readiness_evidence: Hosted replay: on 25/10/26 an unverified harness (Cursor on macOS, BOOKING_AGENT_REPLAY unset, so the general rollout) ran CLI 0.11.2 with skill 0.58.2, installed from the release commit's source folder before publication, so the signed-release check on the first flow init was not exercised. The skill was loaded unchanged from booking-agent skill print. Booking 1 was the $1 AC Repair at HVAC-Koby for Tue 27 Oct 2026, 10:00-11:00 AM MST, at 3194 West Rome Street, Yuma AZ 85364. The saved Google Calendar connection had expired; the user reconnected it through the local sign-in in events mode, and availability found no conflicts. After the slot was chosen the conversation was replaced by a new Cursor chat. Asked "what's going on with my booking?", it resumed that booking at the summary with no second search, no second Link sign-in, and no reconnect request.

Hosted replay: the user said yes; "Booking it now." came at once, the Link approval URL was posted once, and the chat noticed the approval with no further message. $1.00 was charged once (booking fa63d017-8967-40b6-8349-fb082996141d, order 80643a06-726b-4f28-918d-e2ef9701c54b). The booked message included the raw Google Calendar event link, and flow status then returned the same message.

Hosted replay: booking 2 started signed out of Link (flow logout first). flow init sent the assistant to the Link sign-in before any question, the sign-in URL was posted once, and the booking continued when the background poll saw the approval. Google Calendar was connected again through the local sign-in, and availability removed 4 slots that conflicted with the calendar, including booking 1. The $2 AC Diagnostic & Inspection at HVAC-Koby, paid at the appointment, for Tue 27 Oct, 11:00-11:45 AM MST, showed the recap with "$2.00, paid to the business at the appointment (nothing is charged now)". flow book stopped for the business's payment terms and terms-of-service link; after the user accepted them, checkout completed with no Link payment and nothing charged (booking 08a23ee3-e216-4e7d-8cd9-06ea40d4c011, order c7a3b6c4-36fa-4532-9c31-f2bff8090226). The booked message included the calendar link and "Nothing was charged. Full price, due at your appointment."

Hosted replay: both throwaway bookings were then cancelled, and both calendar events were reported deleted. HVAC-Koby did not refund the $1.00; the message gave the refund steps with the booking and order references. flow status on the paid booking said it is cancelled and did not say the user is booked. runtime doctor reported healthy true with one info finding, not_persistent, because ~/.booking-agent on this Mac is not linked to a declared persistent folder.

Hosted replay caveat: the restart was a new conversation on the same machine and filesystem, not a fresh sandbox, so surviving a wiped runtime was not shown on the general rollout. Not run: the connector and delegated calendar routes (Muse ran the delegated route on 0.11.1), a deposit, and bank verification.
The release owner confirmed on 25/10/26 that the fault-report support service has been redeployed and smoke-tested and that pay-at-appointment is generally available on the business side.
The changes in 0.10.2 ship in 0.11.2, which the replay above ran. 0.10.2 is recommended so CLIs before 0.11.2, which stop at the first deferred release, can reach 0.11.2.

Held back until the general replay of 0.11.2 on 25/10/26. Earlier note: Not ready to offer: this release has not been replayed in a hosted session. Base44 Superagent replays of 0.10.1 on 22/10/26 stopped at two defects after a sandbox wipe that kept the saved folder: (1) the new conversation found no linked state, ran `flow init --no-persistent-root`, and started a new booking that asked for a second Link sign-in although the saved booking (waiting for the user's yes) and the sign-in were intact; (2) a rehearsal of the fix then reached the summary, and reconnecting the expired Google Calendar token sent the booking back to the calendar step, dropping the chosen time and listing times again. Nothing was booked or charged.

Offline: `flow status`, `flow init` (with or without `--no-persistent-root`), and `runtime doctor` find an unfinished booking in a persistent folder this CLI prepared earlier and point at `runtime prepare --persistent-root <folder>`; linking that folder brings the waiting booking back at the summary step; a folder this CLI never prepared is not treated as saved state; a calendar connect or skip after the time is chosen keeps the booking where it is and points at `buyer resolve`, while the same step early in a booking still leads to availability. The tests fail without the change; the full suite passes.

Existing businesses and the registry stay compatible: no USP, UCP, or platform profile version changed and no request shape changed. Saved session files are unchanged: no field was added and the format version stays as it is.

Hosted replay (base44-superagent): on 22/10/26 Base44 Superagent installed the published CLI 0.10.2 from PyPI with the wheel's signature check passing (skill 0.57.4 matched its release-tag file; `gh` is not installed there, so the skill file's own attestation was not checked), then booked a $1 HVAC-Koby AC Repair. After the summary was shown, the sandbox was wiped except the saved folder `/app/.agents` (the session file's sha256 was identical before and after), and a fresh conversation reinstalled the CLI, found the saved booking, re-showed the same summary with the chosen 11:45 AM slot, and needed no second Link sign-in, new search, or list of times. The user said yes, accepted the business's terms, and approved the payment in Link; the $1.00 was charged once.

Hosted replay (base44-superagent): Google Calendar was connected. The saved calendar token dropped at the summary and was reconnected without losing the chosen time. `flow status` returned "You're booked: AC Repair with HVAC-Koby, Thu, Oct 22, 11:45 AM - 12:45 PM MST (9:45 - 10:45 PM IDT on your Google Calendar). At your address, 3194 West Rome Street, Yuma AZ 85364. Added to your Google Calendar:" followed by the raw calendar event link. `runtime doctor` reported survived_restart true (basis boot_id_changed), healthy true, and no findings.

Hosted replay (base44-superagent) caveat: Superagent's first closing message paraphrased the booking and left out the raw calendar event link; it posted the CLI's exact booked message only when asked. The CLI returned the message correctly, so this is the harness's wording, not the release.

Hosted replay (base44-superagent) caveat: this host has no control to reset its sandbox, so the restart was an agent-run wipe of everything under /app except /app/.agents, plus /tmp and /root (symlinks into the saved folder removed first), together with a natural boot-id change; it is not the platform reset the replay describes.

Hosted replay (base44-superagent) caveat: the pay-at-appointment path that the 0.9.1 notes list as unreplayed was not run on this harness. HVAC-Koby's current services (a $1 repair, a free diagnostic, and a $10 deposit) do not offer it. 0.10.0 and 0.10.1 carry this replay's record too, since this release includes all their changes, so an installed 0.10.0 or 0.10.1 is offered this one; 0.9.1 and earlier stay deferred for Base44 Superagent.

Earlier replays of 0.10.0 and 0.10.1 on this harness stopped at the defects 0.10.2 fixes (the saved booking could not be shown again after a restart; a calendar reconnect at the summary dropped the chosen time); nothing was booked or charged in them.

Not replayed on Grok Bot. Grok Bot's installed CLI 0.10.0 stops its update walk at the first release with no recommended record for this replay, so without this record it is never offered 0.11.2, the first release that skips a held-back release instead of stopping at it. This record exists only so that walk reaches 0.11.2.

Existing businesses, the registry, and saved session files stay compatible: no USP, UCP, or platform profile version changed in any release from 0.10.0 to 0.11.2, and saved session files keep their format version.

user_summary: After a restart, the assistant finds your saved booking and Link sign-in again, and reconnecting Google Calendar no longer makes you pick the time again.
